optimizationPolicy.method: Price the source recipe per serving, calculate target meal cost divided by source meal cost, and use that ratio as the starting quantity multiplier. Scale protein, carb bases, vegetables, cheese and other substantial ingredients close to the multiplier. Keep serving-defining items practical and adjust potent seasonings, oils and sauces by taste rather than blindly over-scaling. If the source is above the cap, scale down intelligently while protecting protein, food quality and useful volume.
optimizationPolicy.sourceServingRule: Every ingredient in the source recipe is first normalized from the creator's stated serving count to the selected Fuelr batch size. Quantity_selected = Quantity_source × (selected meals ÷ source servings). This applies to protein, carbs, vegetables, cheese, sauces, oils, salt, spices, seasoning packets, and every other listed ingredient.
optimizationPolicy.budgetScalingRule: After serving normalization, calculate the source cost per meal and the current Fuelr meal-cap ratio. Budget multiplier = Fuelr meal cap ÷ source cost per meal. Use that multiplier to increase or decrease the complete recipe while preserving the creator's ingredient ratios and flavor balance. Nothing is left at the source amount just because it is a seasoning.
optimizationPolicy.formulaExample: If a 10-meal source uses 2 tbsp seasoning, the unoptimized amounts are 1.4 tbsp for 7 meals, 2.8 tbsp for 14, and 4.2 tbsp for 21. Every listed ingredient follows the same source-yield conversion before budget optimization.
optimizationPolicy.note: Salt and strong seasonings are never ignored: they scale with the batch. Final amounts may be rounded to practical kitchen measurements, but the 7/14/21 math starts from the source yield.
optimizationPolicy.weeklyMealRule: Each user chooses 7, 14, or 21 prepared meals per week. The calendar has 7 breakfast slots and 14 lunch/dinner slots. A 21-meal week is therefore built from 7 breakfast meals plus 14 lunch/dinner meals, or other compatible 7-meal batches that respect those slot limits.
optimizationPolicy.dynamicMealCapRule: The per-meal cap is personal: school-year food budget ÷ academic weeks ÷ selected weekly prepared meals. Changing from 14 to 21 meals lowers the per-meal target unless the user increases the budget. Fuelr dynamically adjusts optimized recipe quantities toward the user's current cap.
optimizationPolicy.batchSizingRule: A source recipe can be written for any yield. Fuelr normalizes every listed ingredient from the creator's source serving count to the selected 7-, 14-, or 21-meal batch. The catalog stores an optimized 14-meal base; 7 is one-half and 21 is one-and-a-half times that base before applying the user's live meal-cap adjustment.
optimizationPolicy.calendarRule: Fuelr includes a Monday-through-Sunday calendar with Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner slots. Breakfast recipes stay in Breakfast. Lunch/Dinner recipes can move between Lunch and Dinner. A weekly plan can contain at most 7 breakfast meals and 14 lunch/dinner meals.

recipes.name: Hot Honey Steak Hash Brown Burritos
recipes.macrosStatus: Fuelr estimate after scaling the creator-posted 731 cal / 64g protein / 68g carbs / 22.5g fat source burrito
recipes.optimizationNote: The estimated source build was about $4.93 per meal, so the budget multiplier is roughly 1.13×. Fuelr keeps one tortilla per meal but pushes the filling about 15% higher to use the full $5.58 cap: more lean steak, hash browns, cheese and the same flavor profile. This keeps the burrito high-quality and turns the spare budget into more actual food instead of a separate produce allowance.

ingredients: 1.5 kg frozen hash brown potatoes, oil free

ingredients.note: about 7.6 lb; top round or sirloin tip for quality/value

ingredients.item: Frozen hash brown potatoes, oil free

shopping.item: Frozen hash brown potatoes, oil free

instructions: Trim the steak well and cut it into small bite-size pieces so the filling distributes evenly.
Cook the hash browns until browned and crisp. Keep them fairly dry so the burritos do not get soggy.
Cook the steak in batches over high heat until browned and cooked to your preferred doneness. Add the diced jalapeños near the end.
Mix the measured yogurt butter and hot honey into the steak mixture, or portion them evenly across the selected batch.
Lay out one tortilla per meal. Divide the hash browns, steak mixture and cheese evenly so every burrito is a full athlete-sized meal.
Roll tightly and toast the seam side down if desired. Cool before packing.
For a 7-meal prep, refrigerate what you will eat within 3–4 days and freeze the rest if needed. For 14 meals, freeze later-week burritos and thaw in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Loaded Buffalo Chicken Subs
recipes.portion: 2 heavily stuffed sub segments per meal
recipes.macrosStatus: Fuelr estimate after increasing the existing optimized build toward the $5.58 meal cap; creator source was 481 cal / 43g protein / 39g carbs / 17g fat per smaller sub
recipes.optimizationNote: The previous Fuelr build was about $4.86 per meal, so the budget ratio is about 1.15×. Because the bread already defines the two-sub meal, Fuelr spends the extra budget mostly on useful filling: chicken rises to about 4.74 kg for the full batch, with proportionally more cheese and ranch. The result stays the same buffalo-sub idea but gives you more protein and food volume for the full meal cap.

ingredients: 4 baguettes, hollowed and cut into 3 segments

ingredients.note: about 10.45 lb; increased to use the meal cap on protein
starting point; stop earlier if flavor is strong enough
hollow interiors, cut into 3 segments; 28 segments used for 14 meals

instructions: Trim the chicken thighs and cut them into bite-size pieces. Toss with buffalo seasoning, starting below the full scaled amount and adding more until the coating tastes right.
Cook the chicken in batches using only a light coat of avocado oil spray. Brown well and cook through.
Hollow out the baguettes to remove excess bread from the center, then cut each baguette into 3 sub segments.
Build enough sub segments for your selected meal count, loading them heavily with buffalo chicken and ultra-thin provolone or Swiss. Toast until the bread is crisp and the cheese melts.
Finish with the measured fat-free ranch. One Fuelr meal is 2 sub segments.
For a 7-meal prep, make 14 sub segments. For a 14-meal prep, make 28 sub segments; any spare bread segments can be frozen.
Refrigerate the first 3–4 days of cooked portions. Freeze later-week portions and thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.
